source_note: Conservative, qualitative geriatric prescribing decision support compiled from the AGS Beers Criteria (2023 update) and STOPP/START criteria (version 3, 2023). Criterion text is paraphrased for decision support and is NOT a verbatim reproduction. The age threshold for screening is 65 by default (the population these frameworks target). Verify every flag against the current published criteria and clinical context before acting.

beers.rationale: Highly anticholinergic; clearance reduced with age. Risk of confusion, dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention. Avoid as a hypnotic.
beers.recommendation: Avoid in adults ≥65. Prefer a non-anticholinergic agent; for allergy use a second-generation antihistamine.

beers.rationale: Strongly anticholinergic and sedating; orthostatic hypotension and fall risk.
beers.recommendation: Avoid in adults ≥65. If an antidepressant is needed, prefer an SSRI/SNRI with monitoring.

beers.rationale: Increased sensitivity and decreased metabolism of long-acting benzodiazepines in older adults; risk of cognitive impairment, falls, fractures, delirium.
beers.recommendation: Avoid in adults ≥65 for insomnia/agitation. Taper rather than stop abruptly; treat underlying cause.

beers.rationale: Benzodiazepines increase risk of cognitive impairment, delirium, falls and fractures in older adults.
beers.recommendation: Avoid routine use in adults ≥65; reserve for specific indications (e.g. severe GAD, procedural). Taper if chronic.

beers.rationale: Adverse events similar to benzodiazepines (delirium, falls, fractures); minimal improvement in sleep latency/duration.
beers.recommendation: Avoid in adults ≥65. Use non-pharmacological sleep measures first.

beers.rationale: Prolonged hypoglycaemia risk in older adults.
beers.recommendation: Avoid in adults ≥65. Prefer a shorter-acting agent (e.g. glipizide) or an alternative class.

beers.criterion: Beers 2023: NSAID (indomethacin has highest CNS adverse effects)
beers.rationale: GI bleeding/peptic ulcer risk, acute kidney injury, fluid retention; indomethacin has the most CNS effects of the NSAIDs.
beers.recommendation: Avoid chronic use in adults ≥65 unless other options ineffective and with gastroprotection. Prefer paracetamol.

beers.rationale: High GI bleeding and acute kidney injury risk in older adults.
Anticholinergic burden; confusion, sedation, anticholinergic toxicity.
beers.recommendation: Avoid in adults ≥65; prefer a second-generation antihistamine.

beers.criterion: Beers 2023: peripheral alpha-1 blocker for hypertension
beers.rationale: High risk of orthostatic hypotension; not recommended as routine antihypertensive in older adults.
beers.recommendation: Avoid as an antihypertensive in adults ≥65; acceptable for BPH with caution.

beers.rationale: Greater toxicities (thyroid, pulmonary, QT) than other antiarrhythmics; avoid as first-line for atrial fibrillation unless heart failure or LVH.
beers.recommendation: Avoid as first-line for AF rate/rhythm control in adults ≥65 unless specific indication.

beers.rationale: Anticholinergic; confusion, dry mouth, constipation, falls; cumulative anticholinergic burden.
beers.recommendation: Use with caution / avoid in adults ≥65, especially with other anticholinergics or cognitive impairment.

beers.rationale: Sedating, anticholinergic; confusion and fall risk.

stopp.criterion: STOPP v3: antiplatelet without an established indication
stopp.condition_note: Flag when used for primary prevention without documented cardiovascular disease.
stopp.rationale: Aspirin for primary prevention in older adults: bleeding risk often outweighs benefit.
stopp.recommendation: Review the indication. If primary prevention only, reassess against bleeding risk; deprescribe where benefit is unclear.

stopp.criterion: STOPP v3: digoxin as first-line in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
stopp.rationale: Limited benefit; narrow therapeutic index and toxicity risk in older adults, especially with renal impairment.
stopp.recommendation: Review indication and dose; verify renal function and serum level (see also renal dosing assessment).

stopp.criterion: STOPP v3: PPI at full therapeutic dose for >8 weeks without indication for maintenance
stopp.rationale: Prolonged full-dose PPI without ongoing indication: C. difficile, fracture, hypomagnesaemia, B12 deficiency risk.
stopp.recommendation: Review duration/indication; step down to lowest effective dose or deprescribe if no maintenance indication.

start.criterion: START v3: statin therapy with documented atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
start.rationale: Statins reduce cardiovascular events in older adults with established ASCVD where life expectancy is reasonable.
start.recommendation: Consider starting a statin if documented ASCVD and not already prescribed, absent contraindication or limited life expectancy.

start.criterion: START v3: ACE inhibitor (or ARB) in heart failure and/or ischaemic heart disease
start.rationale: RAAS inhibition improves outcomes in heart failure with reduced EF and proteinuric kidney disease.
start.recommendation: Consider starting an ACE inhibitor/ARB if indicated and not prescribed, with renal function and potassium monitoring.

start.criterion: START v3: beta-blocker in stable systolic heart failure and/or post-myocardial infarction
start.rationale: Evidence-based beta-blockers reduce mortality in HFrEF and after MI.
start.recommendation: Consider starting an evidence-based beta-blocker if indicated and not prescribed, absent contraindication.

start.criterion: START v3: bone antiresorptive / vitamin D in osteoporosis or prior fragility fracture
start.rationale: Antiresorptive therapy plus vitamin D reduces fracture risk in osteoporosis / after fragility fracture.
start.recommendation: Consider starting bone protection (with calcium/vitamin D) if osteoporosis or prior fragility fracture and not prescribed.

disclaimer: Decision support only — not a substitute for clinical judgement. Criteria are paraphrased from the AGS Beers Criteria (2023) and STOPP/START v3 (2023) and may not reflect the most recent published update. PIM and omission flags depend on the full clinical picture (indication, life expectancy, patient goals, prior trials). Always verify against the current published criteria and a pharmacist or geriatrician before changing therapy.
